originalProposal:
Hebrews 13:17 calls believers to respond faithfully to those who lead them, because those leaders watch over souls and will give an account. This is not a light responsibility. A pastor cannot faithfully shepherd an undefined crowd in the same personal way he shepherds the people entrusted to his care. The passage calls for both responsible leadership and a congregation willing to receive biblical guidance.

I am called to shepherd the local church God has placed in my care. For me, that is Cedar Grove. This is not permission to ignore people beyond our church. Of course we should answer questions, offer help in a crisis, and share Jesus with those who do not yet belong to our congregation. But I must not neglect the flock I have been called to feed and lead. If I lead our people well, we can serve others far beyond what one pastor could accomplish alone.

Membership gives practical clarity to that relationship. It helps a congregation and its leaders know who is committed to walking together, receiving care, and bearing responsibility. Our ultimate Shepherd is Jesus Christ. Every pastor serves under Him, and no leader's authority can replace the authority of His Word.
